subject: Next steps: streaming latency ceilings & GPU sizing for reserved pool
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Gomez <sofia.gomez@finlytics.com>, Liam Carter <liam.carter@finlytics.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 18:12:00 -0400
Subject: Follow-up: streaming latency ceilings & reserved GPU sizing

Hi Sofia / Liam —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — good conversation. I wanted to capture the performance targets you confirmed and outline the sizing options we discussed so the procurement/engineering teams at Finlytics can review quickly. Below is a concise recap and immediate next steps.

Recap of targets you shared
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~200 inference requests/sec (average).
- Burst allowance: up to ~450 req/s for short windows (1–3 min).
- p50 latency target (streaming responses): <= 30ms per token.
- p95 latency target (end-to-end single-turn): <= 120ms.
- p99 latency requirement (hard): <= 250ms — this is the SLA floor you escalated on the call.
- Concurrency: typically 180 simultaneous sessions, but sessions are short (~6–12 tokens streamed on average).
- Model: you plan to use a proprietary fine-tuned variant of redwood-chat-v1-8k-int8 for production.

Sizing options (high-level)
We ran a set of internal microbenchmarks with that model class and streaming enabled. These are directional estimates to inform a reserved capacity quote:

Option A — H100 (40GB) optimized, high throughput - Single GPU estimated sustained throughput (streaming): ~80 req/s (typical session profile)
- Expected p99 end-to-end under target load (with continuous batching + KV caching): ~180–220ms
- Recommended reserved pool: 3 GPUs to hit steady 200 req/s with headroom (3 * 80 = 240 req/s).

Option B — A100 (40GB) well-balanced
- Single GPU estimated sustained throughput: ~55–65 req/s
- p99 observed: ~210–260ms (depends on burst characteristics)
- Recommended reserved pool: 4 GPUs (4 * 60 = 240 req/s), better cost balance if H100 is constrained.

Option C — L4 / inference-oriented (quantized int8)
- Single GPU estimated sustained throughput: ~100 req/s for smaller models (but for your fine-tuned 8k context it is closer to ~70–90 req/s)
- p99 observed: ~200–240ms when using quantized kernel paths; more variance on large tokens
- Recommended reserved pool: 3 GPUs with careful monitoring; best when you want lower cost per token but accept tighter headroom.

Notes on streaming behavior, batching, and SLOs
- Streaming tokens: continuous batching reduces CPU/GPU overhead for many concurrent short sessions, but it adds micro-batching latency. Our runtime keeps batch windows adaptive; we can tune batch threshold to trade p50 vs p99.
- KV cache hit-rate: for multi-turn flows KV caching reduces end-to-end work significantly. If your sessions reuse context a lot, effective throughput per GPU increases ~15–30%.
- Tail latency: p99 is sensitive to burstiness. We recommend reserving an additional 15–20% capacity (or a 1-GPU burst node) to avoid SLA violations during traffic spikes.

Cost direction (monthly reserved) — very approximate
- H100 baseline: higher unit cost but fewer GPUs.
- A100 baseline: middle ground.
- L4 baseline: cheaper per GPU but may need more units depending on tokenization and context size.

Immediate proposed next steps
1) Finlytics to share a small sample of production-like traffic (anonymized) — you mentioned a 30-minute capture that reproduces session length distribution. I attached finlytics-sample-traffic.json as a placeholder for where to upload.
2) Redwood will run a targeted validation: 2-hour continuous load test + 3x burst scenarios (2min/3min/5min) against the model variant using your traffic shape — outcome: recommended GPU type, recommended reserved pool size, expected p50/p95/p99 numbers. Target delivery: 4 business days after we receive the sample.
3) If Finlytics wants an SLA-backed committed pool, we’ll produce a pricing sketch and a minimal contract addendum (Priyom to own procurement & billing details).
4) Optional: schedule a 30-min engineering session to walk through tuning knobs (batching window, stream flush thresholds, KV cache configs).

Attachments: redwood-slo-gpu-sizing-v1.pdf (detailed notes), finlytics-sample-traffic.json (upload placeholder).

Can you confirm that the targets above match what you expect (especially the p99 hard ceiling)? If so I’ll kick off the validation run and loop in Priyom for the quote.

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber

Subject: Re: Follow-up: streaming latency ceilings & reserved GPU sizing

Thanks Jonas — this lines up well. A couple quick clarifications: 
- p99 250ms is the absolute maximum; we prefer to keep p95 below 120ms as you captured.
- Our sessions average 9 tokens streamed; however about 30% of sessions trigger one longer turn (35–60 tokens) for personalized summaries.
- We can provide a 30-minute anonymized capture by EOD tomorrow.

Also, on the GPU tradeoffs: if H100 gives us the headroom with fewer nodes that helps our ops footprint, but procurement prefers to avoid supply risk. We’ll need pricing sketches for H100 vs A100 vs L4 so we can do a quick TCO calc.

Sofia

Subject: Re: Follow-up: streaming latency ceilings & reserved GPU sizing

Sofia — quick engineering notes for clarity: 
- For the longer-turn 35–60 token sessions we should test with a conservative 12k context to ensure KV cache and attention kernels behave similarly to production.
- We'll run three model variants in the validation: base redwood-chat-v1-8k-int8, a quantized variant tuned for L4, and a fallback lightly-quantized H100 binary — that will show tradeoffs in p99 tails.
- For burst management, we propose configuring an auto-burst node (ephemeral, on-demand) that can spin in <2 minutes to handle the 3–5 min bursts you described. That will reduce committed spend while protecting the p99 SLA.

Priyom — once Jonas confirms we have the capture from Finlytics we should size the quote and draft the reserved-pool pricing sketch. I’ll include the suggested autoscaling/burst policy in the proposal.

Vanessa

Perfect — thanks for the fast turnaround. Action items I’ll take ownership of: 
- Receive and validate the anonymized traffic capture (Sofia).
- Kick off the 2-hour validation run + bursts once validated (Vanessa + engineering).
- Deliver validation report + recommended reserved pool sizing and preliminary quote (Jonas/Priyom) in 4 business days.

I’ll schedule the 30-min tuning session for next week and share a calendar invite. Priyom, I’ll pull draft numbers for H100/A100/L4 options and drop them into the HubSpot deal and the shared Drive link.

If anything changes on targets (especially the p99 ceiling), please flag immediately.

Cheers,
Jonas
